## 5 Reasons Why Developers Prefer Dragonfly Cloud Over Momento Cache

### #1- Superior Performance at Scale

Dragonfly delivers 25x higher throughput and 12x faster snapshotting compared to Redis, making it ideal for high-performance, data-intensive applications. Momento's serverless model limits performance and scalability.

### #2- Significant Cost Savings

Dragonfly's usage-based pricing and efficient architecture result in up to 80% lower costs than alternatives. Momento's serverless pricing can be prohibitively expensive for larger organizations with high throughput needs.

### #3- Seamless Redis Compatibility [...] | Operational Simplicity | Vertical scaling reduces operational complexity compared to clustering/sharding required by alternatives | Serverless model simplifies operations but limits customization options |
| Compatibility | Full Redis compatibility with all data structures and APIs for seamless migration | Momento is not Redis-based and has more limited capabilities compared to Dragonfly |
| Reliability | Built-in replication, persistence, automatic failover, and self-healing ensure high availability | Serverless reliability depends on cloud provider SLAs |

results.title: Memanto - Memory Agent for AI Coding Agents and Fleets | AI/TLDR
results.content:
Retrieval runs on Moorcheh's semantic engine, which Memanto manages for you in one of two ways: a local on-prem stack in Docker (optionally with Ollama for embeddings and answers, no account or API key) or the hosted Moorcheh Cloud, which needs a Moorcheh API key and has a free tier. memanto config backend switches between them. The Memanto code itself is MIT-licensed, and its memories can be exported as the Open Knowledge Format, a plain-Markdown bundle, or migrated in from Mem0, Letta, Supermemory, Zep and Hindsight. The team reports 89.8% on LongMemEval and 87.1% on LoCoMo in its accompanying arXiv paper, and itself cautions that such scores are not comparable across projects.

## // What it does [...] Conflict detection and interactive resolution (memanto conflicts), plus an optional nightly job for daily summaries, conflict detection and expiry sweeps
 Policy-driven expiry with presets and per-type retention tables; expired memories stay recallable, labelled, and restorable
 Grounded answers from stored memory with memanto answer, extraction from chat logs with --from-conversation, and file upload for PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV and Markdown
 Portable estate: export to the Markdown-based Open Knowledge Format and migrate from Mem0, Letta, Supermemory, Zep, Hindsight or an OKF bundle

## // Getting started

Memanto needs Python 3.10+. The first run asks you to pick a backend: On-Prem (Docker, no account or API key) or Moorcheh Cloud (a Moorcheh API key, free tier available). [...] | MemPalace | ★ 60.6k | Local-first agent memory that stores conversations verbatim instead of summarising them, with a structured palace index, pluggable vector backends and an MCP server. |
| OpenViking | ★ 42.4k | A context database that stores an agent's memories, resources, and skills as one browsable viking:// filesystem with three-tier (abstract/overview/details) on-demand loading. |
| Cognee | ★ 33.4k | A graph-native memory engine that turns raw documents and conversations into a queryable knowledge graph for agents that need to build lasting knowledge. |
| Graphiti | ★ 32.9k | A library that builds a temporal knowledge graph from an agent's conversations and data so facts can be tracked and queried as they change over time. |

## Why developers switch to Memanto

### ⚡ Writing memory is free and instant [...] ## Security & sovereignty

 Nothing leaves your machine in on-prem mode. Docker + Ollama, no account, no outbound calls. The whole loop (extraction, consolidation, reconciliation, briefing) runs locally.
 Scoped by default. Each agent gets its own namespace. Your production-ops agent doesn't read your scratch experiments.
 Auditable. Every belief can be traced to where it entered the fleet and when. That's the difference between an auditable memory and a black box.
 Forgetting is a decision, not a side effect. Expiry is policy-driven and reversible. Deletion is a separate, explicit act.
 Deploy it your way. pip, Docker, Compose, systemd or Kubernetes, against cloud or on-prem. `memanto config backend` switches between them, and your memory comes with you.
